title: Embedding latency fabric: mini-batcher + kernel edge tuning
creator: Maya Patel
description: Objective: reduce p95/p99 tail latency for the embeddings endpoint across common batch sizes (1-64). We will prototype a lightweight mini-batcher at ingress that groups short-window requests into deterministic micro-batches, paired with a kernel-edge tuning pass that prefers lower-latency kernels for short sequences and falls back to cost-efficient kernels for large batches. Goals: p99 <= 60ms for typical 768-dim model on provisioned instance types and stable p95 across bursty traffic patterns.
acceptance_criteria: p99 embedding latency measured at frontend (ingress -> response) falls to <=60ms on baseline synthetic traffic matching QPS profile A (70% small, 30% medium)
no increase in token-level inference error or embedding vector variance >2% compared to control (quantization/fallback cases excluded)
end-to-end throughput does not regress by more than 10% under steady-state 100qps workload
change gated behind feature flag and covered by canary rollout with rollback hooks
steps: Build lightweight ingress mini-batcher that holds up to 8ms and composes micro-batches (max size 32) with priority for latency-sensitive tenants
Implement kernel-edge selector: runtime hint to prioritize reduced-latency kernels for sequences <128 and limited KV cache prefetch behavior
Create perf harness to replay production traffic samples and synthetic mixes (small/medium/large) in staging
Run a/B canary with 5% of traffic on Dedicated test pool, collect p50/p95/p99, throughput, and error rates
Iterate on batch hold-time and max-mini-batch-size to navigate latency vs throughput trade-offs
Prepare rollout plan and console flags + dashboard panels for observability
experiments: mini-batcher hold=4ms, max_mbatch=16 -> baseline p99: 112ms -> experiment p99: 68ms (improved p99 but throughput -6%)
mini-batcher hold=8ms, max_mbatch=32 + kernel-edge preference -> p99: 54ms, p95: 22ms, throughput -9%
kernel-only (no ingress batching), aggressive kernel for short seq -> p99: 83ms (improvement but unstable under bursts)
quant-fallback enabled for low-priority tenants -> p99: 92ms for quantized path, flagged as separate SLA tier
results_summary: Prototype combining an 8ms ingress mini-batcher and kernel-edge tuning reduced p99 from ~115ms to ~54ms on our staging Dedicated instance for the target model mix. Throughput dropped ~8% under a steady 100 QPS synthetic workload; impact appears predictable and tunable via max_mbatch and hold thresholds. Quantized fallback remains an option for cost-focused tenants but shows higher p99 and should be exposed as a lower-SLA path.
comments: 2026-03-04 Maya Patel: Kickoff - scoped hypothesis: short-hold mini-batcher reduces straggler tail by increasing micro-batch utilization; kernel-edge differentiation prevents long-path kernels from dominating short requests.

2026-03-09 Omar Siddiqui: Kernel-edge selector added; added heuristic based on seq_len and estimated KV cache residency. Test harness replayed 200k requests; tail improved consistently in mixed traffic.

2026-03-10 Leah Park: Canary deployment (5% traffic) started on dedicated test pool. Collecting metrics. Early look: p99 down ~60% for small-seq requests, but observed small throughput regression. Investigating backpressure behavior at ingress queues.
2026-03-11 Maya Patel: QA note - add regression test in performance suite for 'burst-10s' scenario. Also review monitoring alerts for queue depth > 10ms hold to avoid cascading latency.

2026-03-12 Leah Park: Rolled kernel-edge + hold=8ms mini-batcher to internal 20% canary. p99 stabilized at ~54ms. Preparing rollout checklist and opt-out flags for enterprise customers. Planning review with Product tomorrow.
